title: Validator and Repair Effects Under Shared-Initial-Candidate Semantics: A Paired Study of a Guarded LLM→NetOps Pipeline
abstract: We report a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that measured whether a deterministic validator plus a bounded single-repair step can change the actionable outcome when both baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled LLM candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics). The preregistered study targeted retrieval-augmentation (RAG) poisoning attacks, but the executed adapter contract disabled retrievals (retrieval_augmented_generation = false). Under the realized estimand—baseline single-shot validator outcome on a shared sampled candidate versus final guarded outcome after deterministic validation (and permitted repair)—we executed N = 250 synthetic intent→configuration tasks. The deterministic validator judged every sampled initial candidate valid (n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0); no repairs were applied; baseline and guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rates were identical (1.0). Mapping actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms; paired difference = 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable in this run. We reconcile the archived preregistration and execution artifacts, report execution accounting and representative validator traces, quantify the power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈ 0.05 vs. observed 0.0), and discuss construct, internal, and external validity limitations together with artifact-grounded recommendations for follow-up preregistered experiments.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to support NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, staged maintenance workflows, and zero‑touch configuration. Unconstrained LLM generations can violate operational invariants (ordering requirements, reachability, and policy constraints) that threaten network availability or correctness. To reduce that risk, operational proposals typically pair generation with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures (a generate→validate→repair or guarded pipeline) so that only validated, policy-consistent configurations are applied [6],[7],[8].

Prior literature documents both the rapid adoption of LLM-driven NetOps ideas and the persistence of hallucination- and translation-induced errors that motivate tool-augmented defenses [6],[7],[8]. Adjacent-domain studies of RAG pipelines and adversarial poisoning show concrete failure modes (hallucination, poisoned retrieval context effects, and translation bugs) and motivate controlled adversarial evaluations for NetOps pipelines [2]. Benchmarks and task suites (e.g., NetConfEval / NetLLMBench) enable reproducible evaluation but expose construct-validity concerns for operational invariants [9].

We preregistered study candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 to measure whether controlled poisoning of retrieval contexts (RAG) increases actionable misconfiguration rates and whether deterministic defenses mitigate that effect. The preregistration specified a paired confirmatory design with N = 250 tasks and a primary poison fraction of 0.30. The executed adapter contract, however, implemented generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate and retrieval_augmented_generation = false; these execution-time settings change the realized estimand and require explicit reconciliation. The research question actually tested by the archived execution is therefore: when baseline and guarded arms begin from the same single sampled LLM candidate, does adding a deterministic validator plus an at-most-one repair step change the per-task actionable-misconfiguration indicator for synthetic intent→configuration tasks?
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and applied papers (2024–2026) document proposals and prototypes for using LLMs across the NetOps lifecycle, while repeatedly recommending deterministic validators and tool augmentation to reduce factual and constraint violations [6],[7],[8]. Benchmarks such as NetConfEval and NetLLMBench provide task banks and evaluation primitives but leave open construct-validity questions about whether benchmark success maps to operational safety (reachability, policy compliance) [9].

Tool-augmented architectures (LLMs invoking deterministic verifiers or simulators) have been proposed and evaluated in controlled settings; these architectures can improve grounding but introduce engineering tradeoffs (latency, complexity) [4],[5]. Adversarial work in adjacent domains documents that RAG pipelines can be influenced by poisoned retrieval contexts, motivating the specific preregistered poisoning design of this study [2]. The supplied literature contains proposals, frameworks, and controlled demonstrations but not a broad topology-grounded empirical measurement of RAG-poisoning effects on operational invariants; that gap motivated our preregistration and experimental choices.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 with a primary hypothesis (H1) that controlled poisoned retrieval fragments at a primary poison_fraction = 0.30 would increase actionable-misconfiguration rates; a mitigation hypothesis (H2) posited that deterministic retrieval filters would reduce but not eliminate this increase. The preregistration artifact is archived (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest).

Frozen execution contract and recorded runtime fields. The run used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter and requested declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini as recorded in execution/model_configuration.json (artifact path: execution/model_configuration.json; recorded short-hash prefix: a40e96e2...). Critical executed-contract fields archived in that artifact and the execution manifest: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded arms), retrieval_augmented_generation = false (no retrievals were performed), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, task_count = 250, planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, model_calls_used = 250. The model configuration records temperature = null (unset). Explicit note: null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and must not be interpreted as temperature = 0.

Sampling semantics and comparison logic. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics each task produced a single sampled candidate at the shared_initial_generation stage; that same candidate was evaluated under both conditions. Baseline is the validator outcome on the shared candidate; guarded is the final outcome after the deterministic validator and at‑most‑one permitted repair, invoked only if the validator reported a violation. The per-task binary estimand is actionable_misconfig ∈ {0,1} defined as 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION where VALID_CONFIGURATION is the deterministic validator's binary judgment archived per episode. Because both arms begin from the identical sampled candidate, any observed paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair.

Preregistered analysis plan and missingness. Primary confirmatory test: exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes (α = 0.05) with paired bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Primary missingness strategy: complete_pair_primary (exclude any pair with missing condition outputs). The preregistered power calibration assumed baseline actionable-misconfig ≈ 0.05 to detect an absolute paired increase ≈ 0.045–0.06 at 80% power with N = 250; sensitivity analyses across alternative baseline rates and intra-task correlations were archived in the preregistration.

Validators, task bank, and repair policy. Task bank: 250 deterministic synthetic intent→configuration tasks generated by the archived deterministic_netops_task_generator (task_manifest entries archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 produced per-episode VALID_CONFIGURATION judgments and full validator traces archived under execution/scoring/*.json. Repair policy: at most one repair invocation per failing candidate; repair traces are archived when applied. All raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis inputs are recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl and the execution manifest (artifacts archived and listed in the manifest).
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run began 2026-08-31T21:04:12Z and completed 2026-08-31T21:49:56Z (execution manifest). Planned episodes 500 (2 conditions × 250 tasks) were completed; failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call audit in deterministic_reconciliation records hosted_model_call_event_count = 250, cache_miss_count = 250, and stage_counts showing a single shared_initial_generation stage executed 250 times. Model configuration artifact path: execution/model_configuration.json (short-hash prefix a40e96e2...); raw results path: execution/raw_results.jsonl.

Confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) records n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0; guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0. Under actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION both arms have zero actionable misconfigurations; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Analysis artifacts (condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv) confirm no missing pairs or exclusions.

Representative validator traces and repairs. Representative scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000004-baseline.json and -guarded.json; other examples archived) show identical shared_initial_candidate content across baseline and guarded arms, validator_traces with validation_after.valid = true, and repair_applied = false. No repair_provider_trace entries were produced because the guard never invoked repairs. The deterministic_reconciliation artifact records provider_call_audit and confirms cross-condition cache-key reuse was not observed; the single shared generation per task accounts for the identical responses across conditions.

Power and assumption mismatch. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline actionable-misconfig ≈ 0.05; observed baseline = 0.0 violates that assumption and therefore the run lacks sensitivity to detect the originally preregistered RAG-poisoning effect sizes. We report this power/assumption mismatch explicitly and point readers to the archived analysis artifacts supporting this conclusion (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation limited to the executed estimand. Because both arms used the exact same sampled candidate per task and because the deterministic validator accepted every sampled candidate in the synthetic task bank, the guarded pipeline (validator ± permitted repair) could not alter paired outcomes. The archived evidence therefore documents a null effect of validator-plus-repair under these execution semantics and this synthetic task distribution.

What these results do not establish. The run did not exercise retrieval-augmented generation (retrieval_augmented_generation = false), did not permit independent per-condition sampling, and used a single declared LLM and a single deterministic validator on synthetic tasks. Thus the run cannot adjudicate the preregistered RAG-poisoning hypotheses nor generalize to production heterogeneity, vendor-specific device behaviors, or multi-model ensembles.

Reconciliation of archived metadata and deviation reporting. A reviewer observed that archived analysis_results metadata contained deviations_from_preregistration = [] while the run did not exercise RAG. We clarify: the execution adhered to the frozen adapter contract that was active at runtime (artifact: execution/model_configuration.json; short-hash prefix a40e96e2...) which explicitly set retrieval_augmented_generation = false and generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; the preregistration document (artifact: candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1) described the conceptual RAG plan. Because the recorded execution contract differed from the conceptual RAG plan, the run produced results under the executed contract; the archived analysis metadata therefore reports no post-hoc deviation from the executed contract. We document this execution-time realization here and point readers to the model_configuration and execution manifest artifacts that show the contract values used at runtime.

Threats to validity and operational implications. Internal validity: the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json confirm shared_initial_candidate semantics and one shared generation per task, isolating validator/repair effects but precluding detection of effects requiring per-condition sampling variability. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces an explicit rule set and yields detailed final_state traces, but it may not capture vendor-specific subtleties or asynchronous device behaviors; validator completeness is a construct-validity limitation. External validity: the synthetic task bank, single declared LLM (gpt-5-mini), and single validator limit transferability to heterogeneous topologies and multi-model ensembles. Conclusion validity: the homogeneous all-success outcome yields zero variance in the paired outcome and invalidates the preregistered power assumptions.

Artifact-grounded recommendations for follow-up preregistrations. To test the original RAG-poisoning estimand we recommend a follow-up preregistered run that: (1) enables retrieval_augmented_generation and deterministic poison injection at controlled poison_fraction levels; (2) permits independent per-condition generation (generation_semantics != shared_initial_candidate) so baseline and guarded arms can sample different candidates; (3) constructs a provenance-flagged synthetic-poison corpus with containment checks; (4) broadens validators to vendor-aware simulators where feasible; and (5) includes multiple sampling regimes or model variants to measure sampling sensitivity. These recommendations arise from the archived execution accounting and are framed as preregistered changes rather than post-hoc fixes.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment of a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (declared model: gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; retrieval disabled). All 250 shared sampled candidates passed the deterministic validator (n11 = 250); no repairs were applied; the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate is 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable; we reconciled the preregistration and execution artifacts and documented an explicit power/assumption mismatch. Follow-up preregistered runs that enable controlled retrieval augmentation, independent per-condition sampling, broader validators, and multi-model ensembles are necessary to measure guarded pipelines' mitigation potential under adversarial retrievals and sampling variability.

limitations: The executed design used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate with exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across arms; it therefore measures validator/repair effects on the same candidate and cannot detect differences that require independent per-condition generation variability.

Retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); the preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses and dose–response analyses were therefore not testable in this run and are recorded as an execution-time realization documented in the execution manifest and model_configuration.json artifact (short-hash prefix a40e96e2...).

The stored scorer semantics required an explicit mapping to the preregistered estimand: archived VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1 corresponds to no actionable misconfiguration, hence actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. This mapping was applied consistently in all reported analyses.

A single declared LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were used on synthetic tasks; these choices limit external validity to diverse production topologies, vendor semantics, and multi-model ensembles.

The model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling—hosted-model nondeterminism may remain and is logged in archived provider traces. The observed zero-event outcome (no actionable misconfigs) violates the preregistered baseline-rate assumption (≈0.05) and therefore does not constitute a sensitive test of the original poisoning hypothesis.
